self.description: DatetimeIndex — one of the datetime-like index classes this method is implemented for
DatetimeIndex with MonthStart freq, as shown in the examples
self.constraints: st.builds(lambda n: pd.date_range('2011-01-01', periods=n, freq='MS'), n=st.integers(min_value=1, max_value=12))

self.description: TimedeltaIndex — one of the datetime-like index classes this method is implemented for
self.constraints: st.builds(lambda n: pd.timedelta_range('0 days', periods=n, freq='D'), n=st.integers(min_value=1, max_value=20))

self.description: PeriodIndex — one of the datetime-like index classes this method is implemented for
self.constraints: st.builds(lambda n: pd.period_range('2011-01', periods=n, freq='M'), n=st.integers(min_value=1, max_value=12))

periods.description: Positive number of periods to shift by
Negative number of periods to shift by, can be positive or negative
Zero periods shift — zero is an integer, not excluded by doc

freq.description: If None, the index is shifted by its own freq attribute
Offset aliases are valid strings, e.g., 'D', 'W', 'M' etc.

post_condition.source: Shift index by desired number of time frequency increments.
Shift the index by 10 days. >>> month_starts.shift(10, freq='D') DatetimeIndex(['2011-01-11', ...])
post_condition.expected_behavior: assert all(result[i] == self[i] + pd.Timedelta(days=periods) for i in range(len(self)))

post_condition.source: If None, the index is shifted by its own freq attribute. >>> month_starts.shift(10) DatetimeIndex(['2011-11-01', ...], freq='MS')
post_condition.expected_behavior: assert all(result[i] == self[i] + periods * self.freq for i in range(len(self)))

post_condition.source: The default value of freq is the freq attribute of the index, which is 'MS' (month start) in this example. >>> month_starts.shift(10) DatetimeIndex([...], freq='MS')
